symptom: A decision took one @curve, stamped on every outgoing flow; with the true edge running right and the false edge down, the false edge got the true edge's horizontal vectors and was drawn as an S-curve. DESCRIBE printed only the first outgoing flow's curve, so a Studio Pro decision with a curved true edge and a straight false edge did not round-trip, and `@curve(true: …)` was refused (MDL060).
cause: The curve was modelled as the shape of 'the' flow leaving a statement, which a split does not have: it has one per outcome, and the per-branch form @anchor already had was never given to @curve.
fix: @curve(true: (from: …, to: …), false: (…)) on an IF sets each outcome's vectors (an outcome left out is straight; the flat form still curves both). DESCRIBE prints it when the true and false flows are shaped differently, the flat form when they are alike. MDL060 refuses the outcome form on any other statement.
insight: When an annotation describes 'the outgoing edge', check every node kind with more than one: a split's description that keeps only the first flow loses the rest silently, and the rebuild then copies the kept one onto all of them. Verified on 11.14.0: the issue's repro stores 15;0/-30;0 on the true edge only, describe re-execs Unchanged, mx check 0 errors.
test: mdl/executor/decision_outcome_curve_2592_test.go (build, describe round trip, flat-form control, MDL060 off an IF); failed before (true edge straight, no MDL060)
